title: Trump says he switched planes after Nato summit because of possible threat
excerpt:
Watch: Trump tells reporters why he switched planes

President Donald Trump has confirmed that he secretly swapped planes as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month due to a possible threat.

"I go...
body_text:
Watch: Trump tells reporters why he switched planes

President Donald Trump has confirmed that he secretly swapped planes as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month due to a possible threat.

"I go by Secret Service and the military. They wanted me to go in a different flight, different plane," Trump told reporters on Tuesday. "I just have to do what they say."

The revelation comes after reports that Trump boarded Air Force One on 8 July in view of television cameras before being transported to a military aircraft with the help of a catering truck.

The last-minute switch has raised questions about whether those on the decoy plane were left in danger, but Trump maintained on Tuesday the military jet he boarded instead was at "greater risk".

Officials told the BBC's US partner CBS News that the US had detected a credible Iranian threat to fire a missile at the plane.

Journalists and some White House staff on board did not know the US president had been smuggled out as part of an elaborate ruse in response to a possible Iranian threat.

Watch: Was Donald Trump smuggled out of Air Force One in a catering truck?

Trump has previously said he was Iran's "number one target" during the summit in Ankara.

"I guess there was a threat out there," Trump said on Tuesday. "I didn't really ask too much about it. I get a lot of threats."

He added: "I have a lot of threats that you don't know about."

Trump's dramatic plane swap hints at personal stakes of Iran war

Inside the Secret Service 'shell game' to hide US presidents in plain sight

The clandestine manoeuvre last month came a day after the US renewed military strikes on Iran following a breakdown of negotiations between Washington and Tehran to end the war.

Trump had arrived in Turkey aboard a newer Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar, but announced that he would leave on the old Air Force One "for old time's sake".

On 8 July, footage showed him boarding the presidential jet at Ankara airport.

But according to the Washington Post, he slipped off Air Force One on to a catering truck that had been elevated to plane level on the opposite side to where he had boarded.

He was then secretly taken to a smaller C-32A military aircraft - a modified Boeing 757 often used by the vice-president.

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth boarded the C-32A separately using external stairs in an effort to make the flight appear normal, according to the newspaper.

Journalists and some White House staff boarded Air Force One and were reportedly told to close their window shades. They were unaware the president was no longer on board.

A media pool producer who was on the plane said they found it unusual when they were told to keep the window shades down. A photographer briefly opened a shade and reportedly was quickly told to close it.

The producer's comments were detailed in a report from the White House Correspondents' Association on Tuesday.

They also noted there appeared to have been two catering trucks at both the front and back of the plane when the press arrived, and that the media van had been too far back in the motorcade at the airport be able to take a photo of the president boarding.

Watch: Washington Post and AP reporters reveal details of plane swap over Iran threat

Technically "Air Force One" is the call sign for any aircraft carrying the US president.

But on this occasion, the C-32A used the call sign "Reach 18", while the aircraft carrying the journalists continued to use "AF1" in order to keep up the ruse.

Trump then flew to the UK en route to the US, where he reboarded the old Air Force One and was seen descending from the aircraft after it landed at RAF Mildenhall.

It is unclear how he moved from the C-32A back to the legacy jet.

The president then transferred to the new Qatari-donated Air Force One to travel back to Washington.

During that flight, Trump spoke to reporters on board where he noted the threats posed by Iran but did not mention the earlier plane swap.

Asked why reporters had been told to lower the window shades on the plane from Turkey, Trump said at the time: "Because you're probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleazebags we have to deal with."

He said he had a "threat all the time" on his life, and that he is "number one" on Iran's "list".

Jose Zamora, regional director for the Americas for the Committee to Protect Journalists, said in a statement that the Trump administration "has a responsibility to ensure that journalists covering the president are not unnecessarily exposed to danger".

"Reporters should be informed of credible security threats so they can make informed decisions about their safety," he added.

Watch: What is it like to travel on Air Force One with Trump?

title: Dems eye pick-up in Wisconsin swing district as Rep Van Orden set for rematch in key House race
excerpt: Democrat Rebecca Cooke said "no" when asked whether she would support a federal conversion therapy ban during a June candidate forum in Platteville, Wis. (Credit: CD Chair 3rd CD DPW via Youtube - Jun...
body_text:
Democrat Rebecca Cooke said "no" when asked whether she would support a federal conversion therapy ban during a June candidate forum in Platteville, Wis. (Credit: CD Chair 3rd CD DPW via Youtube - June 19)

A former waitress, small-business owner and nonprofit founder won the Democratic primary in Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District on Tuesday, setting her up for a rematch with Republican Rep. Derrick Van Orden.

Rebecca Cooke, raised on an Eau Claire-area dairy farm, defeated former Eau Claire City Council President Emily Berge on Tuesday evening. The win puts Cooke back on the ballot in one of Democrats’ top House pickup opportunities this fall.

It will be Cooke’s third attempt to win the western Wisconsin seat. She lost the 2022 Democratic primary to then-state Sen. Brad Pfaff before securing the party’s nomination in 2024. Van Orden defeated her that November by roughly 11,000 votes, winning 51.4% of the vote to Cooke’s 48.6%.

WISCONSIN DEM TOUTS ENDORSEMENT FROM UNION PUSHING BACK AGAINST CDL CRACKDOWNS ON ILLEGAL ALIEN TRUCKERS

Rebecca Cooke, candidate for Congress in Wisconsin's Third Congressional District, speaks during a town hall hosted by Pete Buttigieg at the La Crosse Center on January 16, 2026 in La Crosse, Wisconsin. (Kayla Wolf/Getty Images)

Cooke has sought to make her working-class background central to her campaign. She grew up on a dairy farm near Eau Claire, has worked as a waitress since she was a teenager and founded the Red Letter Grant, a nonprofit supporting women entrepreneurs. She also previously operated a small retail business and served on the board of the Wisconsin Economic Development Corp. after being appointed by Democratic Gov. Tony Evers.

Her campaign has focused on affordability, health care and the economic challenges facing rural communities, while portraying Cooke as a pragmatic Democrat able to appeal across party lines in a district that includes Eau Claire, La Crosse and much of western Wisconsin.

Cooke entered the primary as the better-funded candidate and with national support from Democrats.

The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) added Cooke to its "Red to Blue" program, which directs party resources toward candidates viewed as viable in competitive districts.

Berge, a mental health counselor and former Eau Claire City Council president, ran as a local alternative to Cooke, arguing voters should have a choice rather than see the nomination effectively decided by national party backing and fundraising. Her strongest base of support was expected to be in and around Eau Claire.

IOWA DEM ADMITS BEING ‘UNCOMFORTABLE’ WITH WHITENESS AS SHE SEEKS TO FLIP COMPETITIVE HOUSE SEAT

Rep. Derrick Van Orden speaks before Vice President JD Vance at Pointe Precision in Plover, Wis., on Feb. 26, 2026. (Getty Images)

The general election is likely to renew scrutiny of Cooke’s personal finances and past political work. Van Orden’s campaign has pressed her to release a financial disclosure that was extended until Aug. 13, two days after the primary. The campaign has argued that earlier disclosures showing income from political consulting and rental properties undercut Cooke’s working-class image.

Republicans have also sought to cast Cooke as a Democratic political insider, pointing to her work on Democratic campaigns and fundraising. Cooke has presented that experience as part of a broader record that includes operating a business, leading a nonprofit and working in the hospitality industry.

MADISON, WI - NOVEMBER 03: Poll worker Rebecca Brandt, center, feeds a voting tabulation machine with absentee ballots in the gym at Sun Prairie High School on November 3, 2020 in Sun Prairie, Wisconsin. The entire gym was dedicated to counting the absentee ballots. After a record-breaking early voting turnout, Americans head to the polls on the last day to cast their vote for incumbent U.S. President Donald Trump or Democratic nominee Joe Biden in the 2020 presidential election. (Photo by Andy Manis/Getty Images)

Van Orden, a retired Navy SEAL who was first elected in 2022, is seeking a third term.

The 3rd district in Wisconsin, a swing state, has leaned Republican in recent presidential elections, but Cooke’s narrow 2024 loss and substantial fundraising have made the race a closely watched contest as Democrats seek to win back the House in November.

The bipartisan Cook Political Report moved the race from "lean Republican" in the last election cycle to "toss up."

title: Iran holds firm on Hormuz conditions as Pakistan’s Naqvi visits Tehran
excerpt:
Trump should ‘take the less bad deal’ and accept Iranian sovereignty over Hormuz: Analysis

Iran has held firm on its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, as Pakistan’s interior minister, Mo...
body_text:
Trump should ‘take the less bad deal’ and accept Iranian sovereignty over Hormuz: Analysis

Iran has held firm on its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, as Pakistan’s interior minister, Mohsin Naqvi, visited Tehran, and the United States and Yemen’s Houthis launched attacks on shipping in the Gulf and the Red Sea.

The developments on Tuesday came as the US-Israel war on Iran showed no sign of ending, despite repeated claims from US President Donald Trump that a deal was close.

Mohsen Rezaei, the newly appointed head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, told China’s ambassador to Tehran that Washington must end its military campaign and release Iranian funds held abroad for a full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

“As long as the US does not change its behaviour and accept Iran’s conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will not be reopened,” Rezaei said, according to Iranian media.

Writing on X, he insisted on an end to the US’s naval blockade on Iranian ports as well as a region-wide ceasefire, including in Gaza and Lebanon.

“IRAN’s message is clear,” he wrote. “The Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the U.S. ends the war and blockade, releases Iran’s frozen assets, and agrees to a region-wide ceasefire, including in Lebanon and Gaza.

“Until all conditions are met, the Strait will remain closed.”

There was no immediate comment from Washington.

Trump has swung between threats of escalation and assurances of an imminent peace deal throughout the conflict.

In an interview broadcast late on Monday, he suggested that the uncertainty could last ⁠for a while, saying he might just “bop along” and let Tehran fail economically, or “hit” them “really, really hard”.

“I’m sort of negotiating,” Trump told Real America’s Voice. “They’re very devious negotiators.”

In Tehran, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Pakistan’s interior minister, with the two sides discussing closer political, economic, trade, cultural and security ties, according to the Iranian presidency.

Naqvi’s visit comes as Islamabad mediates efforts to end the ongoing conflict.

Earlier, Qatar – another mediator in the conflict – said talks between Iran and Oman on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz had reached an advanced stage.

“We have heard positive statements from both capitals in the recent couple of days,” said Majed al-Ansari, spokesman for the Qatari Foreign Ministry. “Our main priority here is the reopening of the strait, maintaining the ceasefire and making sure that we are able to push forward towards the negotiation.”

Iran, meanwhile, said any agreement between it and Oman on routes in the Strait of Hormuz will have no impact on the reopening of the waterway.

Separately on Tuesday, US Central Command said a US Navy MH-60 helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles to disable the steering gear of a Panama-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman.

It said the ship had ignored repeated warnings to stop violating the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

At the southern end of the Red Sea, four crew members were killed in a suspected Houthi attack on a small cargo vessel in the Bab al-Mandeb strait, according to Yemen’s Transport Ministry. Two Yemeni rescuers from an anti-Houthi military group were also killed, Yemen’s coastguard said.

The killings on board the Egyptian-owned Tihamah would be the first by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi strikes on shipping since the war on Iran began in late February.

The Houthi-run Saba news agency reported that the ‌group had attacked a Saudi ship carrying military equipment in Bab al-Mandeb. It did not name the ship, and there was no immediate Saudi response to the report.

Thousands of people have been killed since the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28. Iran has also struck US assets and infrastructure in Oman, Jordan, Kuwait, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia.

In Iran, at least 3,527 people have been killed, while more than 27,00 have been wounded. At least 18 Americans have also died.

The conflict has also widened to Lebanon, where Iran-backed Hezbollah has launched attacks on Israel, and Israeli forces have carried out near-daily strikes.

Lebanon’s Health Ministry says Israel’s latest military escalation there, which began on March 2, has killed more than 4,300 people and injured more than 12,000. In Israel, at least 60 people have been killed in Iranian and Hezbollah attacks.

title: Chiefs receiver Rashee Rice says he is '100% locked in' after serving 30-day jail time for probation violation
excerpt: Before Rashee Rice was back with his Kansas City Chiefs teammates for the upcoming season, he had to serve 30 days in jail following a probation violation stemming from a multi-vehicle crash back in 2...
body_text:
Before Rashee Rice was back with his Kansas City Chiefs teammates for the upcoming season, he had to serve 30 days in jail following a probation violation stemming from a multi-vehicle crash back in 2024.

Rice called the discipline a "reality check."

"It was a learning experience and a reality check," Rice said, via ESPN. "Don’t focus on the past. Focus on what’s going on now. I’m doing [well] mentally."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Rashee Rice walks to the field before practice during Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026, at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Mo. (Icon Sportswire)

Rice was on probation for his involvement in the 2024 multi-vehicle crash, where he eventually pleaded guilty to two felony charges.

The NFL also docked Rice six games for violating their personal conduct policy, which he served this past season.

CHIEFS RECEIVER RASHEE RICE JAILED FOR 30 DAYS AFTER PROBATION VIOLATION AND IT COULD GET WORSE

Rice violated his probation after testing positive for THC, which mandated a 30-day jail sentence in Texas. He began serving that sentence on May 19, and he was released from jail in mid-June.

He also received surgery to take care of loose bodies in his right knee, which caused him inflammation during his eight games for the Chiefs in 2025.

He declined to speak with reporters who were waiting for him outside the detention center, but now at training camp, Rice faced the music.

"It was mentally tough. They gave me ways to communicate with my teammates still as well as my athletic trainer," Rice explained. "Besides the hard times in there, I kept my mind right watching shows and as much Kevin Hart as I could to laugh."

Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice runs after a catch against the Los Angeles Chargers at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Dec. 14, 2025. (TNS)

Rice added that he was allowed to get treatment done on his knee while serving his time as well.

"I would stretch it, do some activation on it and then hit the weight room and jog, just condition and get the muscle fatigue going as well as my stamina."

Rice is only entering Year 4 in the NFL, but off-the-field issues have taken away from the solid chemistry he has with quarterback Patrick Mahomes, who has trusted him with top wide receiver duties. His production has warranted that as well.

"I’m 100% locked in on what’s going on now with the team," Rice explained. "I’m ready to go out there and dominate. I’ve got a good group of brothers behind me."

Wide receiver Rashee Rice #4 of the Kansas City Chiefs is interviewed during the Super Bowl LVIII Opening Night presented by Gatorade featuring the AFC Champion Kansas City Chiefs and the NFC Champion San Francisco 49ers on February 5, 2024 at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Jeff Speer/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Rice tallied 571 yards on 53 receptions with five touchdowns in his eight games with the Chiefs in 2025. He had a breakout rookie campaign with 938 yards on 79 catches with seven scores in 2023, but he was unable to play a full year in 2024 after suffering a season-ending knee injury.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Longtime anti-Trump Dem ousted after tough primary from upstart progressive mayor
excerpt: Rep. John Larson, D-Conn., got into a heated exchange with Fox News’ Chad Pergram over whether the DSA-affiliated candidates who won in New York City's primaries could create headaches for House Democ...
body_text:
Rep. John Larson, D-Conn., got into a heated exchange with Fox News’ Chad Pergram over whether the DSA-affiliated candidates who won in New York City's primaries could create headaches for House Democrats and a possible Speaker Hakeem Jeffries.

Fourteen-term Rep. John Larson, D-Conn., met his match in Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin during Tuesday’s hard-fought primary race.

Larson, who has served in Congress since the Clinton administration, faced three challengers: Bronin, state Rep. Jillian Gilchrest and Hartford Education Board member Ruth Fortune. The sprawling district includes Hartford, Glastonbury, Bristol and Windsor Locks.

Earlier this term, during a markup of legislation providing House members with DOGE access to Treasury payment information, Larson erupted at his colleagues and began yelling:

"You will do whatever Elon Musk and Donald Trump tell you to do. Where's the independence of the committee? Where's the legislature? We're an equal branch of government," Larson yelled. "Look at the empty seats here. Where's Elon Musk?"

HOUSE DEMOCRAT LASHES OUT WHEN GRILLED ON WHETHER SOCIALIST VICTORIES WOULD THREATEN DEM UNITY

Rep John Larson, D-Conn., (left) and U.S. President Donald Trump (right). (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images; Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

Larson has routinely criticized Musk and President Donald Trump during his tenure, notably filing more than a dozen articles of impeachment following the arrest and extraction of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro.

In that case, Larson accused Trump of piracy and other offenses. The impeachment push came as Larson faced a primary challenge from the younger Bronin.

Bronin, who also served in the Obama administration, appeared to be gaining on incumbent Larson as the year went on. He ran as a candidate seeking generational change in a longtime Democratic seat.

STATE OF PLAY: DEMS BATTLE FOR SHOT AT CRUCIAL ARIZONA HOUSE SEAT AMID GOP'S RAZOR-THIN MAJORITY

Democrat Rep. John Larson yells during a House committee meeting about Elon Musk and DOGE. (Fox News)

The First District has not seen a Republican lawmaker since Rep. Edwin May Jr., R-Conn., who served during the Eisenhower administration.

Gilchrest is considered a progressive who also is also pro-choice abortion rights.

Fortune, considered the lowest-funded major candidate, ran an education-focused campaign.

Clockwise from top left, Connecticut Reps. John Larson, Jahana Hayes, Jim Himes and Joe Courtney. (Tom Williams/Roll Call/Kevin Dietsch/Victor J. Blue/Bloomberg/Douglas Healey/Getty Images)

Republican challenger Amy Chai, a medical doctor focused on addiction treatment, said on her campaign site that Americans are too stressed and depressed because of national divisions and need a change.

Democrats, however, are again favored over Chai and the GOP this fall in the district.

Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

title: Bondi shooting hero Ahmed al-Ahmed cleared of assault charges
excerpt:
Al-Ahmed, who maintains his innocence, was accused of putting his father in a headlock in March

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily ...
body_text:
Al-Ahmed, who maintains his innocence, was accused of putting his father in a headlock in March

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The man who disarmed one of the gunmen allegedly responsible for the Bondi beach terror attack has had an assault case against him tossed out.

Ahmed al-Ahmed, 44, had been accused of putting his father in a headlock on 9 March and intimidation over an alleged incident in June.

He pleaded not guilty to both charges in an appearance at Bankstown local court on 24 June, before prosecutors confirmed on Wednesday they had withdrawn both counts.

An apprehended domestic violence order protecting his father will remain in place for 12 months, court documents show.

In June, his lawyer, Mohamad Sakr, emphasised al-Ahmed would maintain his innocence.

“It is a family situation he never expected, one would never want to expect, and it must be really difficult for him,” he said.

“He is a heroic man and his honesty and dignity should be maintained until these matters are ultimately determined.”

When the charges were initially laid, al-Ahmed alleged members of his family were seeking a cut of the $2.5m raised on his behalf after he garnered international attention for his actions during the massacre.

“This situation is untrue, it’s extortion ... and my two brothers have been harassing me, abusing me and pushing to get money from me,” he told Sydney radio 2GB in June.

His brothers, Sameh and Hozifa, were granted conditional bail in June after pleading not guilty to charges of using a carriage service to menace or harass, regarding claims they tried to extort $200,000 from their brother.

An interim domestic violence prevention order prohibits the pair from going within 100 metres of their brother, his home or workplace.

The tobacconist made headlines around the world after video footage of him disarming a gunman during the Bondi massacre went viral.

He was shot in the arm multiple times during the incident and was visited in hospital by the prime minister, Anthony Albanese.

He was awarded the keys to the city of Canterbury-Bankstown, where he lives, and Waverley, where the attack took place.

title: Passenger jet billed as China’s answer to Boeing and Airbus prepares to make first international flight
excerpt:
The Comac C919 will fly from Beijing to Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, although experts say it could take generations for it to challenge the west’s dominance of the industry

China hopes to break into the ...
body_text:
The Comac C919 will fly from Beijing to Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, although experts say it could take generations for it to challenge the west’s dominance of the industry

China hopes to break into the world of commercial aviation with the first international flight of a Chinese-made passenger jet scheduled for Wednesday.

The Comac C919 will take off from Beijing capital international airport at 3pm, landing in Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, just over two hours later.

It has been billed as China’s alternative to the Boeing-Airbus duopoly that dominates global aviation, particularly in Asia, but analysts say it could take generations before a Chinese aircraft could meaningfully challenge their global dominance.

The C919 is made by the Chinese state-owned aircraft manufacturer Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (Comac) and is similar in size to the Boeing 737.

The C919 has been flying on domestic routes operated by Chinese airlines since 2023. But Wednesday’s Air China flight to Ulaanbaatar will be the first time that the narrow-body jet is used on a commercial international route.

“This is essentially a public relations move,” said Scott Kennedy, a senior adviser at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies. “Ulaanbaatar was likely chosen because of how close it is to Beijing. It doesn’t change the fact that the plane was years overdue, is composed of western components, and is less efficient than its Boeing and Airbus cousins.”

China has long dreamed of building its own jet. When the C919 was unveiled in 2015, Li Jiaxiang, the head of China’s civil aviation authority, said: “A great nation must have its own large commercial aircraft.”

But progress has been slow, even while China has whizzed ahead in other hi-tech fields, such as robotics and electric vehicles (EVs).

That is because aviation requires the integration of many different types of advanced science and engineering, as well as parts sourced from overseas. An analysis by the Centre for Strategic and International Studies in 2020 found that more than half of the C919’s suppliers were in the US.

“Large passenger aircraft and jet engines are extremely complex and challenging to manufacture. They require precision components, complex electro-mechanical control systems, and the ability to coordinate a vast global supply chain,” said Kyle Chan, a fellow at Brookings focused on China’s industrial policy.

“There’s a reason there are basically only two major commercial aircraft makers in the world. Building large passenger jets that are safe and reliable is an order of magnitude more difficult than making EVs,” Chan said.

Last year Comac reportedly delivered only 15 units of the C919 to customers, well short of its target of 75.

Comac did not respond to a request for comment.

Comac primarily serves Chinese domestic airlines. In 2023, the Brunei-based airline GallopAir signed a $2bn deal to purchase 30 planes from Comac, including 15 of the C919, but the airline is not operating commercially yet. The C919 has not been approved by European or American regulators.

Last year the US reportedly suspended the export of some products to Comac for use in the C919 jet amid the tit-for-tat restrictions that Beijing and Washington used against each other during the US-China trade war.

The two countries later agreed a trade war truce that is set to expire in November.

When US president Donald Trump visited Beijing in May for a state visit, one of the few takeaways from the trip was an agreement from China to buy 200 jets from Boeing.

In return, the US provided supply guarantees for aircraft engine parts and components for its own manufacturing.

China sees being able to build its own commercial aircraft as a national security priority.

In a recent interview with Chinese state media, Zhang Yanzhong, an academic of the Chinese Academy of Engineering and a leading aviation expert who worked on the C919, said reliance on other countries for large aircraft technology would “threaten national strategic security”.

However, there was still “a long way to go before achieving commercial success”, Zhang said.

Experts have pointed out that Comac’s dependence on foreign suppliers goes beyond the supply of individual components. International suppliers have also provided guidance about how to integrate complex components and software together into sky-worthy commercial aircraft.

Kennedy argued it was misleading to describe the C919 as a Chinese plane because so many of its parts were imported. He said it was “very unlikely” for Comac to become a serious challenger to Boeing and Airbus, “even a generation from now”.

Chan said Comac could still face “a long road to gaining trust among airlines and passengers”.

Zhang called on China’s young engineers to contribute their talents to China’s aviation ambitions, saying: “Though the journey may be fraught with difficulties, a fledgling eagle can soar faster than its parent.”

title: North Korea launches another ballistic missile as US, South Korea prepare for military drills
excerpt: Mark Montgomery, a senior fellow with The Foundation for Defense of Democracies, speaks to Fox News Digital about North Korea recently test-firing a short-range ballistic missile during the U.S. confl...
body_text:
Mark Montgomery, a senior fellow with The Foundation for Defense of Democracies, speaks to Fox News Digital about North Korea recently test-firing a short-range ballistic missile during the U.S. conflict with Iran.

North Korea launched another ballistic missile Tuesday, marking its second reported ballistic missile launch in less than a week.

Japan’s prime minister’s office announced the latest launch Tuesday. Details about the missile’s trajectory, range and where it landed were not immediately available.

The U.S. military said it was monitoring the launch and consulting with allies and partners in the region.

NORTH KOREA EXPERT WARNS US CAN 'NEVER TAKE THEIR EYE OFF' KIM JONG UN FOLLOWING MISSILE TEST DURING IRAN WAR

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un watches a sea-to-surface strategic cruise missile test from the destroyer in an image released by North Korean state media. (KCNA via KNS / AFP via Getty Images, File)

"We are aware of the recent missile launch and are consulting closely with our allies and partners. Based on current assessments, these events do not pose an immediate threat to U.S. personnel or territory, or to our allies," U.S. Pacific Command said in a statement. "The United States remains committed to the defense of the U.S. homeland and our allies in the region."

The latest launch comes less than a week after North Korea test-fired a short-range ballistic missile from its eastern Wonsan area on Aug. 5.

That missile landed in waters off North Korea’s east coast and did not reach Japanese territory, Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said following the launch.

Koizumi said North Korea’s repeated missile launches pose a threat to Japan and the region, and Tokyo lodged a protest with Pyongyang through their embassies in Beijing.

MICHIGAN MILITARY EXERCISE PREPARING THOUSANDS OF TROOPS FOR CHANGING BATTLEFIELD

North Korea test-fired a short-range ballistic missile on Aug. 5. The Hwasong-11LA ground-to-ground tactical short-range ballistic missile is seen being test-fired at an undisclosed location on April 19, 2026, according to the Korean Central News Agency. (KCNA/Reuters)

South Korea’s military bolstered its surveillance posture and coordinated with the U.S. and Japan following the Aug. 5 launch, according to South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff.

South Korea’s presidential national security council called that launch "a provocation" that violated U.N. Security Council resolutions and urged North Korea to stop its missile activity.

The launches come ahead of annual joint military exercises between the U.S. and South Korea, which are typically held during the second half of August.

"This annual exercise aims to build understanding between Combined Forces Command, United States Forces Korea, the United Nations Command, and ROK Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS), ROK government agency, ensuring their ability to fortify the combined defense posture and enhance Alliance response capabilities against a spectrum of security threats," United States Forces Korea has said of the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises.

WHY TRUMP IS DOWNPLAYING REPORTS RUSSIA AND CHINA ARE HELPING IRAN

U.S. soldiers from the 2nd Infantry Division participate in a river crossing exercise as part of the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise last year, in Yeoju-gun, South Korea. (Getty Images, File)

"It will feature live, virtual, constructive and field-based training, engaging personnel from the various military services," it added.

U.S. and South Korean officials have said the training is defensive in nature, while North Korea has characterized the exercises as preparation for an invasion and has often responded to military drills with missile tests.

The Aug. 5 test was North Korea’s first ballistic missile launch since late June, when it tested a tactical ballistic missile carrying what state media described as a "special mission" warhead along with other weapons.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said following those tests that his military needed to bolster its "deadly and destructive offensive posture."

Fox News Digital's Greg Norman-Diamond contributed to this report.

Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: 4-year-old dies after suffering electrical shock from clothes dryer inside Kansas home
excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A 4-year-old child died in a "tragic accident" last Thursday after being electrocuted by a clothes dryer, according to...
body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A 4-year-old child died in a "tragic accident" last Thursday after being electrocuted by a clothes dryer, according to Kansas officials.

The incident happened in Savonburg, Kansas, while the child was "playing" inside a home, the Allen County Sheriff’s Office (ACSO) said in a statement Saturday.

The child "allegedly received an electrical shock from a 220v dryer," the sheriff’s office said.

The parents rushed their child, who was reportedly unconscious, to a local hospital around 9:30 p.m., according to authorities.

GEORGIA TEACHER, FATHER HAILED AS HERO AFTER DYING TO SAVE GIRL FROM MYRTLE BEACH RIP CURRENT

A woman with kids loads clothes into a washing machine.  (iStock)

However, the child was later pronounced dead at the hospital.

No foul play is suspected at this time, and the ACSO is investigating the incident.

Officials extended their condolences to the family and responders involved following the incident.

"The Sheriff’s Office extends our heartfelt condolences to the family members and all those affected by this tragedy, including the Allen County dispatchers, first responders, and hospital personnel," the office said.

A 220-volt electrical current, which was involved in Thursday’s accident, can cause serious injury or death, including cardiac arrest.

MAN, WOMAN KILLED IN RIP CURRENT AS LIFEGUARD SHORTAGE LEAVES DANGER ZONES IN BEACH DESTINATION

While clothes dryers have been linked to thousands of home fires annually, primarily caused by lint buildup blocking exhaust ducts or overheating electrical elements, electrical deaths involving major laundry appliances are considered extremely rare.

In one of the rare instances, a 10-year-old boy was found dead inside a dryer at a Houston-area apartment complex in 2018, according to Fox 5 DC.

A woman removes freshly dried clothes from a household dryer. (iStock)

A medical examiner determined the boy had been electrocuted, while investigators found no signs of injury or foul play.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Republican survives primary on Tim Walz's old congressional turf as Dems eye seat flip
excerpt: Senate Majority Leader John Thune addresses the GOP fundraising shortfall in crucial 2026 midterm races during an interview on 'America's Newsroom.' Thune reacts to Chuck Schumer embracing Democratic ...
body_text:
Senate Majority Leader John Thune addresses the GOP fundraising shortfall in crucial 2026 midterm races during an interview on 'America's Newsroom.' Thune reacts to Chuck Schumer embracing Democratic Socialists of America candidates and analyzes ongoing maritime tensions with Iran. He also weighs in on the confirmation path for Todd Blanche as attorney general, highlighting the narrow margins in the Senate.

Republican voters in Minnesota chose their incumbent representative in the U.S. House as their nominee in the race for the state's 1st Congressional District.

Finstad faced off with Gregory Goetzman and Oliver Morlan in the Republican primary on Tuesday.

Goetzman previously unsuccessfully challenged Finstad in 2024, earning a measly 4.26% of the vote compared to the incumbent's 90.9%. Morlan, who is involved in his family's industrial cleaning business, ran in Tuesday's race as the political outsider.

2026 MIDTERMS: PRIMARIES, KEY RACES AND ELECTION RESULTS

Incumbent Rep. Brad Finstad, R-Minn., faced challengers Gregory Goetzman and Oliver Morlan in the Republican primary. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call/Getty Images)

Of Minnesota's eight districts in the U.S. House of Representatives, the 1st District is one of the state's four Republican-held House seats. It covers a large swath of southern Minnesota, including Rochester and much of the state's farm country.

Finstad will advance to the November general election to face the winner of the Democratic primary between Alex Eaton, a math teacher and former teachers-union leader, and Jake Johnson, a small business owner. Eaton is considered more establishment while Johnson is considered to be the more progressive of the Democrat candidates.

The bipartisan Cook Political Report ranks the race as 'lean Republican,' a downgrade from the 'solid Republican' ranking in the last elections as Minnesota, especially in its city centers, increasingly embraces leftist ideals.

A sign is seen outside a polling place in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on March 3, 2020. (Stephen Maturen/Getty Images)

Rep. Finstad has represented Minnesota in the House since winning a 2022 special election. It was held after Republican Rep. Jim Hagedorn, who after years of therapy and surgery for a kidney cancer diagnosis in 2019 and after testing positive in January 2022 for COVID-19, died on February 17, 2022.

Before Hagedorn, the seat was represented by Democrat Tim Walz, who left Congress after being elected governor in 2018. He is still governor, after an unsuccessful run for vice president on the ticket with then-Vice President and presidential candidate Kamala Harris.

Walz announced on January 5, 2026 he would not seek reelection.

The district has leaned Republican in recent election cycles but has a history of electing candidates from both parties. (Joseph Prezioso/AFP/Getty Images)

Minnesota's 1st congressional district has trended Republican in recent election cycles but has a history of electing candidates from both parties.

Agriculture, health care, manufacturing and the economy are expected to remain central issues as the race moves toward the November general election.

The Republican and Democratic nominees will compete in November to determine who will represent southern Minnesota in the U.S. House.

Amanda Macias covers the intersection of business, economics and politics, with a focus on how policy decisions shape markets, businesses and American workers.

title: Failed presidential candidate wins Dem primary for Midwest governor amid fraud scandal fallout
excerpt:
Sen. Amy Klobuchar outlined her plan Sunday to overhaul Minnesota government and crack down on fraud, while facing criticism from Republicans tying her to Gov. Tim Walz’s record. (Credit: KMSP)

Sen. ...
body_text:
Sen. Amy Klobuchar outlined her plan Sunday to overhaul Minnesota government and crack down on fraud, while facing criticism from Republicans tying her to Gov. Tim Walz’s record. (Credit: KMSP)

Sen. Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn., has won the Democratic nomination for governor of Minnesota as she continues her bid to replace outgoing Gov. Tim Walz, who dropped out of his re-election bid in the midst of a massive fraud scandal.

Klobuchar, Minnesota's senior U.S. senator and a former Democratic presidential candidate, defeated a field of long-shot challengers in Tuesday's Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party primary.

Klobuchar will move on to face the winner of the crowded GOP primary in November.

MN GOVERNOR RACE TO REPLACE WALZ SEES MAJOR SHAKEUP AS GOP CONTENDER ENDS CAMPAIGN: 'DON'T SEE A PATH'

Sen. Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn., speaks during a rally in support of a "Yes" vote on Proposition 50, a congressional redistricting measure in the November 4 special election, at the Los Angeles Convention Center in Los Angeles, California, on Nov. 1, 2025. (David Swanson/REUTERS)

Walz announced earlier this year that he would not seek another term as governor as his administration faced intense criticism over its handling of fraud involving Minnesota government programs that federal prosecutors say could end up costing the taxpayers over $9 billion.

The fraud issue has loomed over Minnesota politics, with Republicans hammering Walz and state Democrats over what they say was a failure to prevent the misuse of taxpayer dollars.

Klobuchar entered the race with significant advantages in name recognition and political experience. She has represented Minnesota in the Senate since 2007 and previously served as Hennepin County attorney.

She also sought the Democratic presidential nomination in 2020 before ending her campaign and endorsing former President Joe Biden.

KLOBUCHAR VOWS FRAUD CRACKDOWN, AUDIT OF MN GOV’T AS GOP BLASTS WALZ TIES

Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz testifies during a House Oversight and Government Reform Committee hearing in the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on March 4, 2026. The hearing examined alleged misuse of federal funds for Minnesota social services and Medicaid programs. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

When she rolled out her governing priorities in May, Klobuchar said: "You are right to be angry about the fraud. It is unacceptable and it must end." She promised a "top-to-bottom audit" of state government beginning on "day one."

The Plymouth, Minnesota born Klobuchar's campaign includes a policy plank titled "Make Government Accountable and Root out Fraud." It says that "fixing the government is the foundation of everything we need to do" and promises "immediate action to root out fraud."

Klobuchar's gubernatorial campaign puts her in the unusual position of seeking a new office without first relinquishing her seat in Washington.

Klobuchar has not resigned from the Senate while campaigning for governor. Her current Senate term does not expire until January 2031, meaning a loss in the gubernatorial race would not by itself cost her the Senate seat.

Sen. Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn., referred to the Minneapolis Catholic school shooter as a "he" in an NPR interview Wednesday, prompting the outlet to clarify it's "unclear" what the shooter's identity is. (Bloomberg/Getty)

If Klobuchar wins the governorship in November and resigns from the Senate, her departure would create a vacancy in Minnesota's congressional delegation.

Klobuchar will now attempt to keep the governor's mansion in Democratic hands in November in a state that has not had a Republican governor since former Gov. Tim Pawlenty left office in January 2011.

Andrew Mark Miller is a reporter at Fox News. Find him on Twitter @andymarkmiller and email tips to AndrewMark.Miller@Fox.com.

title: White House asks DOJ to consider new prosecution in Reflecting Pool case
excerpt:
President Donald Trump blames vandalism for the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool needing costly repairs after viral videos showed paint peeling on the monument.

White House officials have asked the D...
body_text:
President Donald Trump blames vandalism for the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool needing costly repairs after viral videos showed paint peeling on the monument.

White House officials have asked the Department of Justice (DOJ) to explore whether it would be possible to pursue a new prosecution against the man accused of vandalizing the newly renovated Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, weeks after federal prosecutors moved to dismiss felony charges against him, Fox News has learned.

The previous case, which U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro's office moved to dismiss on July 31, accused Olympic canoeist David Hearn of damaging the costly $14 million project after cracks, algae growth and peeling sealant were discovered.

Pirro's office cited findings from the Department of the Interior that concluded the damage was linked to flaws in the installation process rather than vandalism.

White House officials have since reached out to the DOJ to determine whether Hearn could instead face a misdemeanor charge, as first reported by The Wall Street Journal. No final decision has been made, Fox News has learned.

TRUMP URGES JEANINE PIRRO TO REVISIT DROPPED LINCOLN MEMORIAL REFLECTING POOL VANDALISM CASE

President Donald Trump has urged U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro to revisit the recently dropped charges over vandalism at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

In response to the move, Hearn's attorneys said pursuing a new case would only undermine the DOJ's credibility after prosecutors already acknowledged they lacked sufficient evidence to support the original charges.

"If true, it would mark a shocking first: a case that the DOJ lost by its own admission because it lacked the evidence to convict, returning from the dead. This would add another bizarre turn to a sad chapter in the DOJ's history and further harass an innocent man," the attorneys said in a joint statement.

The statement was issued by Norm Eisen of Democracy Defenders Fund, Mary Dohrmann of Washington Litigation Group, and Steve Levin of Steptoe LLP.

TRUMP SAYS HE 'DISAGREES 100%' WITH U.S. ATTORNEY JEANINE PIRRO OVER REFLECTING POOL CASE

Members of the National Guard walk by as workers apply a coat of paint to the Reflecting Pool on the National Mall on Thursday in Washington, D.C. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

While Pirro's office has moved to drop the original federal case, prosecutors sought a dismissal without prejudice, meaning the charges could potentially be brought again.

The possibility of a renewed prosecution comes as the Trump administration has repeatedly maintained that the damage was caused by vandalism.

President Donald Trump said slashes were found in the pool's material that appeared to have been made with a knife. He also claimed people had been seen kneeling at those exact locations with their hands in the water.

U.S. Park Police identified Hearn as a suspect after he was reportedly seen grabbing and tugging on a loose section of the pool's coating on June 19. Police said he continued to do so even after National Park Service employees urged him to stop.

TRUMP DOUBLES DOWN ON REFLECTING POOL VANDALISM ALLEGATIONS, CITES NEW WITNESS ACCOUNT

David Hearn has been accused of damaging the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. He has maintained his innocence.  (David Madison/Getty Images, File; Annabelle Gordon/Reuters)

The damage was estimated at about $1,000 and resulted in Hearn's indictment on July 2 on one count of felony destruction of property.

Trump has urged Pirro to reconsider her "hastily made" decision to drop that felony charge and criticized Hearn's alleged political connections, claiming he was a "big player" in the Democratic fundraising platform ActBlue.

"U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro should re-visit her hastily made decision, especially since it turned out that the ‘gentleman’ involved is a big player in ActBlue, a disgraceful fundraising SCAM, and is represented by a TRUMP DERANGED SLEAZEBAG, Political Hack Lawyer, Norm Eisen, and CREW, a group that uses ‘charity’ for political purposes which is, to the best of my knowledge, ILLEGAL!" Trump said.

Trump later said Pirro "choked" under pressure from a judge regarding the case and "folded like an ​umbrella."

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

The Portuguese striker posted an image on his Instag...

Football superstar Cristiano Ronaldo has married his longtime partner - model and influencer Georgina Rodríguez - in a civil ceremony in Portugal.

The Portuguese striker posted an image on his Instagram account , externalshowing two hands - presumed to be his on top of his wife's - both wearing wedding rings.

Calling it the wedding of the year, Portuguese media say the couple tied the knot on 11 August in the coastal town of Cascais near Lisbon - and that their five children attended.

The Instagram entry had more than 3m likes within 30 minutes of being posted.

The image posted on Ronaldo's Instagram account

The couple have been together for 10 years, after they met at a Gucci shop in Madrid where Rodríguez was working. He was playing at the Spanish club Real Madrid at the time.

They announced their engagement on 11 August last year.

At the time, Rodríguez posted a picture of a large ring, writing "Yes I do. In this and in all my lives" in her native Spanish.

Ronaldo has scored nearly 1,000 goals in a career in which he has played for Lisbon-based Sporting, Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus, Al Nassr in Saudi Arabia and Portugal.

He recently played in his sixth World Cup, a record for appearances in the men's finals which he shares with Lionel Messi of Argentina.

title: ‘The Office’ star Lucy Davis ‘at peace’ with 'incurable' cancer diagnosis after nearly ignoring warning sign
excerpt:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Lucy Davis revealed a devastating Stage 4 breast cancer diagnosis after quietly battling the disease for the past year and a half.

...
body_text:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Lucy Davis revealed a devastating Stage 4 breast cancer diagnosis after quietly battling the disease for the past year and a half.

"The Office" actress said the cancer had metastasized to her spine, right hip and ribs and was now "incurable," with chemotherapy no longer an option.

"The initial lump that I felt, wasn’t a ‘lump’ as such; rather a kind of hard spot. Really tiny," she wrote on Instagram. "I almost didn’t bother getting it checked. So I guess I’m saying don’t ignore anything – get everything checked out."

Rather than dwell on her prognosis, Davis said she was determined to embrace whatever time she had left.

BARRY MANILOW RESCHEDULES CONCERT 45 MINUTES BEFORE START AMID ONGOING LUNG CANCER RECOVERY

‘The Office’ actress Lucy Davis is opening up about her private battle with incurable Stage 4 breast cancer – and the subtle symptom she almost ignored. (Frederick M. Brown/Getty Images)

"As of now, I’m trying to live out whatever might be left of my life in as fun a way as I possibly can," she explained. "I always like to find the teachable moments in anything negative that happens. And cancer has not disappointed in that regard; there’s a lot I have learned from it, and I’m grateful for that."

Davis said maintaining that outlook had not made the physical realities of cancer any easier.

"As some of you will know, the pain can really be something else," Davis wrote. "Standing and walking for too long a time can be hard, and I need to use a wheelchair sometimes (so if you see me toddling around in one, feel free to give me a push!)"

Despite the pain, Davis said she had found peace with what could come next.

"The Office" star Lucy Davis says she’s choosing joy, purpose and peace as she continues acting and advocating for animal rights amid her cancer diagnosis. (Kevin Winter/Getty Images)

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I’m not scared of whatever comes next," she said. "I’m at peace with it. I’ll see my Gracie sooner than expected, and for me, leaving my physical body just means going home. Any and all grieving is for my family; it’s far harder for them than for me."

But Davis made clear she had no plans to stop pursuing the work and causes she loved.

"I’m still going to keep up all my work for animal rights," Davis noted. "It’s so important to me. And I still would like to keep working. I’m perfectly able to do so, and acting is one of the biggest joys in my life."

After an 18-month battle kept largely out of the public eye, Lucy Davis shared an emotional update on cancer’s physical toll and the outlook keeping her going. (Dave Benett/Getty Images)

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Simon Pegg, Lucy Davies and Nick Frost attend the U.K. premiere of "Shaun of the Dead" on March 30, 2004. (Dave Benett/Getty Images)

Davis began acting in the 1990s, with an early role as Maria Lucas in the BBC’s acclaimed 1995 adaptation of "Pride and Prejudice." Her major breakthrough came as receptionist Dawn Tinsley in Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant’s original British version of "The Office," which ran from 2001 to 2003 and became an international comedy phenomenon.

Davis later built a career spanning British comedy and major Hollywood productions including, "Shaun of the Dead," "Wonder Woman," "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina" and "The Villains of Valley View."

title: Paramount escalates threat to leave California as Dem AG's antitrust lawsuit stalls Warner Bros merger
excerpt: NewsBusters executive editor Tim Graham tells Fox News Digital that Paramount CEO David Ellison’s recent essay about making CNN "straight down the middle" didn’t do him any favors with the network’s l...
body_text:
NewsBusters executive editor Tim Graham tells Fox News Digital that Paramount CEO David Ellison’s recent essay about making CNN "straight down the middle" didn’t do him any favors with the network’s liberal staffers.

Paramount's new chief is threatening to move his studio out of California if the Golden State's attorney general doesn't come to the table to resolve the high-stakes antitrust lawsuit.

Puck News reported Tuesday that Paramount CEO David Ellison is serious about relocating his headquarters to a more business-friendly state like Georgia, Tennessee or Texas if California AG Rob Bonta, who is leading 11 other states to block Paramount's $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), doesn't negotiate a settlement by Oct. 1. According to the report, Ellison is "in contact" with multiple states.

Ellison, who will soon be forced to pay WBD a multimillion-dollar "ticking fee" if the merger stays in limbo, remains convinced that Paramount would be victorious in court — except the antitrust trial isn't taking place until March 2027, meaning his company will have to likely fork over at least $650 million quarterly to WBD if nothing is settled until next spring.

PARAMOUNT-WARNER BROS DISCOVERY ANTITRUST TRIAL DATE SET; MERGER PUT ON PAUSE OVER LEGAL BATTLE

Paramount became the first major film studio to speak out against a widespread boycott of Israeli film institutions on Thursday. (Erik McGregor/LightRocket)

According to the report, Ellison could move Paramount — and potentially Warner Bros. if he ultimately merges both companies — out of California "regardless of the eventual outcome of the case." Ellison has even developed a five-year plan that would relocate the vast majority of jobs out of the state while still maintaining a footprint in Hollywood.

Bonta slammed the latest Paramount buzz, renewing his accusation of attempted "blackmail" by the studio.

"In a span of weeks, Paramount agreed to halt the merger until a court decision or until June 2027, asked for a November trial, and is now back with another attempt to blackmail the state into letting an illegal deal through. Paramount has lost the plot as it continues to lose in court," Bonta wrote on X. "It didn't work the first time — on the eve of our July lawsuit — and it won't work this time."

"This illegal merger will result in higher costs, fewer options, and fewer people making movies. My office remains committed to stopping illegal consolidation and protecting a vibrant California economy for businesses that play by the rules," he added.

CALIFORNIA AG ROB BONTA FACES ‘POLITICAL FAVOR’ CLAIMS OVER NETFLIX-LINKED $1M TRAIL IN PARAMOUNT SUIT

Attorney General Rob Bonta speaks during a news conference in Sacramento, Calif., Tuesday, Sept. 26, 2023. California's attorney general will not seek criminal charges against a police officer who in 2020 fatally shot a man outside a pharmacy in the San Francisco Bay Area amid national protests over the police killing of George Floyd, his office announced on Dec. 19. (AP Photo/Rich Pedroncelli,File)

However, while speaking at a Politico conference later in the day, Bonta did signal a willingness to negotiate with Paramount if "structural remedies" are implemented by the company.

Bonta's lawsuit claims the merger would "lead to higher prices, lower quality, and less content for film and television, harming movie theaters, basic cable distributors, and ultimately, audiences on every sofa and movie theater seat in the U.S."

The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District for the Northern District of California, claims the merger violates Section 7 of the Clayton Act, which holds that mergers that may substantially lessen competition or tend to create a monopoly are illegal. Both sides argued their case last week but Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín waited until Monday to temporarily delay the merger.

The merger, which was set to close this year, is now being delayed until at least June 2027.

Bonta has faced accusations of a conflict of interest from his Republican challenger for California attorney general, Michael Gates, who questioned whether a financial connection to Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings' family influenced Bonta's decision to bring the lawsuit.

"Rob Bonta has turned his taxpayer-funded office into a favor factory for his political bosses and donors. He's pursuing politically-motivated litigation against a competitor for a company that's bankrolled his PAC," Gates told Fox News Digital.

Campaign-finance records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Hastings' wife, Patty Quillin, contributed $1 million to Smart Justice California Action Fund on March 16, 2022. The independent committee was working to boost Bonta and other progressive prosecutors.

Netflix was previously in negotiations to purchase Warner Bros. Discovery before Paramount made its offer.

CNN STAFFERS SEE PARAMOUNT MERGER AS 'INEVITABLE' DESPITE LEGAL BATTLE DELAYING ELLISON TAKEOVER

(Noam Galai/Getty Images for Paramount) (Noam Galai/Getty Images for Paramount)

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

Paramount's bid to buy Warner Bros. Discovery would be a historic deal merging two major Hollywood studios under one corporate umbrella as well as all of their television networks, including CBS and CNN. Critics of the deal believe such a merger would crush the entertainment industry and lead to mass layoffs. Some have also been vocal against Ellison and his billionaire father, Larry Ellison, who is heavily financing the deal and is a close ally to President Donald Trump.

Liberal critics in particular also claim that, as a result of the deal, CNN would be given a MAGA-bent to its coverage, and it would be run by current CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss, who has been harshly criticized by some media liberals. The Paramount CEO has previously assured that CNN would maintain editorial independence following the merger.

In an op-ed published in The New York Times, Ellison addressed the "speculation" about what would happen to CNN under his ownership.

"I have regularly voted for candidates of both parties; I hold some views that would be called conservative and others that would be called liberal, just like most Americans; and when it comes to our news operations, I do not aspire to lead these companies to bend their newsrooms to my views. I believe that news should be based on facts and truth," Ellison wrote.

"Great news organizations like CNN and CBS News are here to tell it straight down the middle," he added. "That requires newsrooms that reflect the whole world, not one side of it. And it requires independence."

The deal would follow Ellison's $8 billion purchase last year of Paramount, merging the studio with Skydance Media.

Fox News Digital reached out to Paramount and Bonta's office for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Fox News' CJ Womack contributed to this report.

Joseph A. Wulfsohn is a media reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to joseph.wulfsohn@fox.com and on Twitter: @JosephWulfsohn.

title: Fever coach Stephanie White launches fiery defense of herself after Sophie Cunningham hit
excerpt:
DiJonai Carrington went to Threads to claim "white privilege" following her takedown flagrant foul of Sophie Cunningham despite her intentionally clotheslining her in the face.

When Chicago Sky guard...
body_text:
DiJonai Carrington went to Threads to claim "white privilege" following her takedown flagrant foul of Sophie Cunningham despite her intentionally clotheslining her in the face.

When Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington hit Sophie Cunningham on Saturday, pundits predictably turned on Cunningham. Meanwhile, Fever coach Stephanie White stayed quiet.

White has stayed similarly quiet when Caitlin Clark has absorbed physical hits and media fire. Heading into Tuesday's game against the New York Liberty, White took the podium and suddenly found plenty to say.

DiJonai Carrington of the Chicago Sky was ejected after a brutal foul on Sophie Cunningham of the Indiana Fever. (Kamil Krzaczynski/Imagn Images)

"You know, this isn't necessarily for those people that are in this room. This is more for an online community that's trying to create narratives that simply don't exist. Trying to create a fabrication or distortion of who I am, of what I'm about. Our players' success, our players' health and wellness, our players' safety is always a top priority for me. One of the things I pride myself on is my relationships with players."

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT AGAINST DIJONAI CARRINGTON AFTER FLAGRANT FOUL AND 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' POST

White brushed off criticism as a fabricated narrative while Cunningham absorbed the heat.

Sophie Cunningham #8 and head coach Stephanie White are shown during a game against the Toronto Tempo at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Ind., on June 16, 2026. (Getty Images)

"For those who have anything to say about the play in the last game? I didn't see the play in real time. I went straight to a press conference. I thought the play got called right. Thankfully, Sophie's okay. Was it egregious? Absolutely. When you have a chance to watch that over and over and over on replay, you can see that. I didn't have that in real time."

Missing the hit live explains Saturday night. It doesn't explain the silence that followed.

FEVER COACH STEPHANIE WHITE DODGES QUESTION ON GOP LETTER ABOUT CAITLIN CLARK’S TREATMENT IN WNBA

"I take personally any suggestions that I don't 100% always have my players' back. I ride with them 10 toes down all the time, all of the time. They know that. It's a shame that we can't have an opportunity to talk about what great basketball they're playing because they are f***ing playing."

Riding "10 toes down" rings hollow when Cunningham was left to absorb the backlash after Carrington's hit. Clark has faced similar moments before her. Then came the moralizing.

White added, "The reality is with me, I will always lead with love. I will also lead with grace. I will always lead with humility. And I will always lead with integrity. Doesn't mean I'll always get it right. I'm also human."

Nobody attacked her humanity; they called out her passivity. White then framed the criticism as something more sinister.

LET'S HAVE AN HONEST CONVERSATION ABOUT CAITLIN CLARK, RACISM, AND MEDIA COWARDICE

She continued, "The hate, the fear-mongering, the divisiveness, the stuff that's trying to hijack our league will not win. It won't win. We are united. We are connected. We will not be divided. Every day, these women put their a** on the line. Every day. When they go low, we go high. Love will win, grace will win. Humility will win and kindness will win. I stand by them, I will always stand by them. Everybody else can go to hell."

After the news conference, Fever president Kelly Krauskopf soon issued a statement backing White.

"Coach White has done a tremendous job leading the Fever and for the second-consecutive season, has us in great position for a playoff push. She has kept our team focused and united, all while under the brightest spotlight our team and our league have ever experienced. She has the full support of leadership."

The statement backs White. But it doesn't answer the criticism.

Cunningham took the hit and the backlash that followed. By the time White finally called Carrington's play "egregious," much of her response was spent defending herself.

That's not riding 10 toes down. That's showing up after the fight is over.

Head coach Stephanie White and Caitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever meet during the second quarter against the Connecticut Sun at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Indiana, on June 17, 2025. (Dylan Buell/Getty Images)

Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

title: CBS Sports president says 'no timetable or final decision' on Tony Romo's future after OWI arrest
excerpt:
Fox News national correspondent Kevin Corke reports on Tony Romo’s refusal to take a breathalyzer test on ‘The Will Cain Show.’

Tony Romo’s status with CBS remains a fluid situation, but the presiden...
body_text:
Fox News national correspondent Kevin Corke reports on Tony Romo’s refusal to take a breathalyzer test on ‘The Will Cain Show.’

Tony Romo’s status with CBS remains a fluid situation, but the president of CBS Sports said "there is no timetable or final decision" following his OWI arrest last month.

CBS Sports president David Berson spoke at "NFL on CBS" Media Day on Tuesday, where he was asked about Romo, who was placed on indefinite leave by the network. J.J. Watt was named as CBS Sports’ top analyst alongside play-by-play legend Jim Nantz on gamedays ahead of the 2026 NFL season.

The announcement came after Romo was arrested by Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office deputies after showing signs of impairment while driving in Wisconsin on his way back from a golf event.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Tony Romo speaks to police on bodycam footage during traffic stop that led to arrest. (Milwaukee County Sheriff's Office)

"It’s an evolving situation and we are still assessing," Berson replied to the question about Romo. "There is no timetable or final decision at this time.

"I hope you can respect and appreciate this is a personal matter and a legal one for Tony."

A follow-up question asked Berson why he was placed on leave as the legal situation played out.

"We have to consider the impact on our image and our brand," he replied. "That’s very important to us. The focus should be and needs to be on our presentation and this great product and not on any others.

"Fortunately, we have a deep bench and everybody is stepping up."

Romo was charged with operating while intoxicated after performing poorly during field sobriety tests. He was also charged with having an open bottle of alcohol in his vehicle and with unsafe passing.

CBS Sports play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz (left), analyst Tony Romo (center) and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson at press conference at the Super Bowl LVIII Media Center at the Mandalay Bay Resort and Casino on Feb. 6, 2024. (Kirby Lee/USA TODAY Sports)

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Romo is in the middle of his massive 10-year, $180 million deal with CBS as their top NFL analyst, and he is reportedly still owed $72 million after signing the deal in 2020.

OutKick reported in late July that Romo’s future with CBS is in jeopardy beyond his leave, as there were doubts prior to his arrest about whether the network would keep him as its lead analyst after the 2026 season. It’s also worth noting CBS will be airing the Super Bowl in 2028.

Debate about Romo’s preparation has come up in recent seasons, especially among critics saying he hasn’t gelled with Nantz like in years past.

It’s also been reported that Romo’s contract has an industry-standard morals clause, which CBS could invoke to fire Romo over the arrest video. His legal team, though, would almost certainly fight that with millions still owed.

Tony Romo on "The Drew Barrymore Show" ahead of Super Bowl LVIII. (Gail Schulman/CBS via Getty Images)

Romo’s court date has been set for Sept. 21, which comes eight days after CBS Sports’ first NFL broadcast.
